title: AFP confirms Chinese bomber plane sighting 170 nautical miles from Manila
summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Wednesday confirmed the sighting of a Chinese bomber plane near the shores of Luzon or 170 nautical miles away from Metro Manila.

blocks.text: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Wednesday confirmed the sighting of a Chinese bomber plane near the shores of Luzon or 170 nautical miles away from Metro Manila.
AFP spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad was asked in a briefing regarding a Chinese H-6 strategic bomber reportedly seen in the West Philippine Sea.
Trinidad confirmed that the AFP monitored the plane.

“It only shows that the PLA (People's Liberation Army) … is now flexing its muscles. Sa baka dati-rati ang mga patrols niya were closer to the mainland of China. Today, mas umaabot sa atin,” Trinidad said during the Kapihan sa Manila Prince Hotel briefing.
(It only shows that the PLA (People's Liberation Army) … is now flexing its muscles. So before these patrols were closer to the mainland of China. Now, it is closer to us.)
“That bomber was 170 nautical miles from Metro Manila. The closest it got to our shorelines was, I think, 45 nautical miles,” he added.
GMA News Online sought comment from the Chinese Embassy and will publish it as soon as it is available.
Despite the bomber plane’s close proximity to the country, Trinidad said there was no reason for concern.
Trinidad said that there was no indication that the plane was practicing for a missile attack.

“It was a normal patrol conducted by the H-6 bomber. It has been conducted in the past over flights by bombers of the PLA Air Force over Scarborough Shoal, Bajo de Masinloc… There is no indicator that there was such a rehearsal for a missile strike,” Trinidad said.
Trinidad said that the AFP has already been able to modernize their capabilities to the point where they are able to monitor such aircraft before it enters the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone.

The Philippines and China have a longstanding row over the West Philippine Sea. Beijing has claimed most of the disputed waters for itself, despite the Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling that upheld Manila’s Exclusive Economic Zone.
China has consistently shown aggressive behavior in the disputed waters by blasting Philippine vessels with water cannons and tailing boats dangerously. —NB, GMA News
